theorem_title: Large-denominator approximation under a uniform power-law approximation hypothesis
natural_language_statement: Let ν and X be real numbers with ν > 0. Assume that for every natural number Q there are an integer p and a natural number q such that Q ≤ q and |π − p/q| ≤ q^(−ν). Then there are an integer p and a natural number q with 2 ≤ q, X < log q, p ≠ 0, and |π − p/q| ≤ q^(−ν). The approximation hypothesis is part of the theorem's assumptions; this statement does not assert unconditionally that such approximations exist.
explanation: Choose a natural N with exp X < N, then apply the assumed approximation statement with Q = max(2,N). The resulting denominator q satisfies q ≥ 2 and q ≥ N, hence exp X < q and X < log q. If p = 0, the approximation inequality would give π ≤ q^(−ν) ≤ 1, since q ≥ 1 and ν > 0; this contradicts π > 3. Thus p ≠ 0, and the same approximation bound is retained.
